conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning, Mr. ___. I'm Dr. ___, one of the surgical team members. You're here today because of a recurring pressure sore on your sacrum. We’ve scheduled surgery later today to clean it out and close it with a flap. How are you feeling this morning?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Morning, doc. I’m okay, just tired. The pain’s been worse lately, especially when I shift in the chair. Is this going to fix it for good?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re doing a V-Y advancement flap, which has a good success rate. But because you’re paraplegic and can’t move easily, pressure sores can come back. The key is using an air mattress and not putting pressure on that area after surgery.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had this done before. Last time it came back in a few months. I just don’t want to keep going through this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. We’ll do everything we can to make this one last. You’re on a good pain regimen, and we’ll keep you off the area for at least three weeks. Your plastic surgeon will follow up closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright. And what about my nephrostomy? I’ve been spiking fevers again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your urine test showed signs of infection. We found Morganella morganii, which can be tricky. We wanted to change your nephrostomy tube while you’re here, but you mentioned you didn’t want that done.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t want them poking around with that again. Last time it hurt for days. Can’t I just take antibiotics?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can treat the infection with antibiotics, and we’ve started you on cefazolin IV. But without changing the tube, the infection might not fully clear. It’s the best way to prevent future fevers.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll think about it. But for now, I just want to get through the surgery.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Understood. We’ll focus on the sacral wound today. The anesthesiologist will see you soon. Try to rest before the procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Mr. ___, you’re back in your room. The surgery went well. We removed the infected tissue and closed it with a flap from your buttock. You’re on a PCA pump for pain—press the button if it gets uncomfortable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks, doc. I feel groggy, but no sharp pain. Is the flap going to hold?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It looks good so far. Blood flow is strong. The next 48 hours are critical. We’ll keep you on bed rest and monitor it closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the drain? I feel something pulling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a small drain to remove fluid from the site. It helps the flap heal. We’ll teach you how to empty and record the output before you go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs are stable. Hemoglobin is a bit low at 8.1, but that’s expected after surgery. Your kidney function is stable—creatinine is 3.7, which we’re watching.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that bad? My kidneys have been off for years.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s consistent with your stage 4 CKD. We’re avoiding nephrotoxic drugs. That’s why we chose cefazolin—it’s safer for your kidneys.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve got enough problems without my kidneys crashing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re also giving you heparin shots to prevent clots, since you’re not moving much. And we’d like you to sit up in the chair tomorrow if you can.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll try. But I’ve got pain in my back and shoulders from sitting so long.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can adjust your pain meds. You’re on oxycodone as needed. Let the nurse know if it’s not enough.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your urine culture came back. It’s Morganella morganii, which is sensitive to several antibiotics, including ciprofloxacin and gentamicin. But again, without changing the nephrostomy, the infection may persist.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know, I know. But I don’t want the tube changed here. Can’t I just take the pills?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can switch you to oral cefadroxil, which covers this bug. But please follow up with urology soon. This isn’t something to ignore.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll call them when I get home. Just get me through this recovery first.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Fair enough. Your flap is looking good—warm, pink, no signs of infection. You can start advancing your diet today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’m tired of broth. Any word on when I can go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If all goes well, possibly tomorrow or the next day. We need to see your drain output go down and make sure you’re comfortable on oral pain meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. Your drain output is decreasing—only 25 mL yesterday. That’s a good sign. We’ll likely remove it tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’ll be a relief. Can I shower with it still in?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, but keep the site clean and dry. Let the water run over it, then pat dry. Don’t submerge it. And keep the drain secured so it doesn’t pull.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And I need to write down how much drains out each day, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Bring that log to your follow-up. Also, keep using the air mattress. No sitting or lying on your back for at least three weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember. Last time I didn’t, and it opened up. I’m not doing that again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. Watch for redness, swelling, or darkening of the flap. If it turns blue or black, call your surgeon immediately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about my seizures? I haven’t had one in months, but I’m on levetiracetam.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re still on your regular dose. We haven’t changed any of your home meds except for pain and antibiotics. Keep taking them as prescribed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my depression meds? Escitalopram and trazodone?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’re getting those too. We know mental health is part of recovery. If you’re feeling down or anxious, let us know.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m okay. Just ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Mr. ___, you’re cleared for discharge. Your vital signs are stable, you’re eating well, and the drain output is low. We’ll remove the drain before you leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Finally. What do I need to do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Use the air mattress, keep the area clean and dry, monitor the incision, and record any drainage. Take cefadroxil twice a day for ten days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my nephrostomy? I’ll call urology, I promise.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Please do. You had a positive urine culture and fevers. This infection won’t go away on its own. Follow up within a week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And I’ll see plastic surgery next week?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, in seven to ten days. Call sooner if you have fever, increased pain, or flap changes. You’re going home with services—nursing will check on you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks, doc. I’ll take care of this one. I don’t want to be back here soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re rooting for you. Take it slow, follow the instructions, and keep in touch. You’re doing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Appreciate it. Tell the team thanks for taking care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I will. Have a safe trip home. We’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One more thing—what about that lung nodule? Should I get it checked?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, as before, a follow-up CT in three months. Your primary team will coordinate that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll schedule it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. And keep taking your sevelamer with meals for your phosphate levels.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I haven’t missed a dose. My nephrologist would kill me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Smart. Alright, I’ll sign your discharge orders. The nurse will go over everything one more time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks again, doc. I mean it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, Mr. ___.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will be in shortly to remove the drain and finalize discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—keep up with your bowel regimen. We started you on something to help prevent constipation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I’ve had issues before. I’ll keep using it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. That’s all for now. Rest well at home.
